svg.text: Flywheel hosted — design C, your account and our control plane: every machine in your account
a design, not a tier of A.34

we provision the same binary into the customer's own account through a role that trusts our OIDC issuer, and keep only a registry, a deployer and the identity environment · the price is blind support: we cannot see what broke, and we say so rather than ask for a copy
YOUR SIDE, AND THE THIRD PARTIES · the same in all three designs
GitHub
your account, your repositories
the state repository · the blueprints repository · your code repositories
plaintext, yours — under GitHub's own encryption, as every repository is
the App is installed on your organization; its token is scoped to the listed repos
your laptop host
optional · intermittent
the page on localhost · local adapters · worktrees
unchanged — and moving here is not a migration
closed past its stale window it shows away: leases stand and their clocks pause
Slack or Discord
your workspace, your own app and bot
Discord free text is a slash command option; plain replies need a socket
nobody holds · Slack free text arrives over the Events API
the bot is yours here, matching security.md (e): no shared component of the chat path remains
Frontegg
the hosted tiers' sign-in
sign-in, membership and roles for the served name
its token is verified on every page and tool call (249)
device flow with GitHub stays the self-managed path (A.32)
THE MACHINES · all of them in your AWS account · we keep no store, no queue and no cache
page and tool server
request-invoked · not a tick
your AWS account
the same function in your account, behind your own served name
it verifies the Frontegg token on every call (249) — the identity token
replaces the private network as the boundary
the page is a static bundle; the tools are the binary's own catalogue over HTTP
a request is a read, never a tick · a write from the page enqueues instead
capture receiver
API Gateway and a receiver function — in your account
your AWS account
your key encrypts the queue and your account holds it
a receiver function verifies the signature, answers Discord's PING and
routes by workspace id · stateless, and here it is yours too
your queue raises a content-free wake — only the org id; the tick reads it under your role
dispatcher function
the same binary, running in your account
your AWS account
we provision it through a role you create that trusts our OIDC issuer
it assumes your role, runs one tick, wipes its scratch, and exits
it interprets chat and triages self-contained captures in-process:
one bounded model call per message · model access under the assumed role,
metered into the plan, or a key you place
only triage over the raw material a capture points at, and elaboration and
construction, run on a laptop or a pool host
woken only through your queue: the receiver, the scheduler and a page write
all enqueue, so one tick of yours runs at a time
a tick has 15 minutes; triage yields to the interpreter
the sandbox is reused across organizations; scratch wiped and the data key
dropped before exit
scheduler
EventBridge Scheduler · in your account
your AWS account
60-second precision · at most one entry per organization
create-or-update, deleted after it fires · it enqueues, it never invokes
warm cache
one S3 object per organization — in your bucket
your AWS account
a git bundle of two sparse shallow clones, under your own key
state, and blueprints restricted to the manifest, the claims and flywheel/
we keep nothing warm at all — there is no cache of yours on our side
pool host
created from your image, in your account
your AWS account
baseline up to 8 GB / 4 vCPU, bursting to 32 GB / 16 vCPU, 32 GB of disk
no VPC needed, and Docker runs inside it, so devcontainer features work
your pools, at whatever bound you set, on your own quota
no co-tenant exists to isolate from, because no account is shared
its image is built on a pool host or your machine, never in the dispatcher
triage over pointed-at raw material runs here or on your laptop
registry
organization names, tier, health, counters
our service account
deployer
a stack applied through your role, our binary version stamped
our service account

health · counters · readings (288)
WHO OWNS THE ACCOUNT EACH MACHINE RUNS IN
in our service account
the registry, the deployer and the identity environment — names, tier, health, counters, and provisioning
in your AWS account
the receiver and its queue, the page and tool server, the dispatcher, the scheduler, the cache, the pool hosts, the key, your raw store
on your side and the third parties
GitHub, the laptop host if you run one, your own chat app and bot, and Frontegg
WHAT WE CAN TELL THE CUSTOMER
“If you would rather we held nothing at all, we provision the whole thing into your account and keep only your organization's name, its tier, its health and its bill.
There is no co-tenant, no shared process, and no cache of yours on our side — and the chat app is yours too, so no shared component of the chat path remains.”
what stays ours is the supply chain: our binary runs in your account
